The Court made the following Order  Order:
 The writ petition is filed seeking direction to the respondents not to invoke the old Land Acquisition Act basing on the Award No.111/82 dated Sri.Ghadiyaram Siddartha Sankar Das vs State Of Ap., Revenue Dept., 4 Others on 8 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84637127/
1 16.08.1982 of the 4th respondent as no physical possession obtained and no compensation paid to the petitioner or his father for Ac.0.34 cents situated at Pernamitta Village, Santhanuthalapadu Mandal, Prakasam District situated in Survey No.150 Part and to invoke Section 24 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and  2 Resettlement Act, 2014 and also to issue interim direction to the respondents not to interfere with the subject matter land, without following due process of law, pending disposal of the above writ petition.
2.

sentences.text: The writ petition is filed inter alia

stating that the petitioner's father is the owner of an extent of Ac.4.17 cents situated in different survey numbers i.e.,
118 Part, 149 Part, 150 Part, 153 Part of Pernamitta Village.

In the year 1982 when the petitioner's father was alive, the 4th respondent passed an Award No.111/82 dated 16.08.1982 reflecting the petitioner's father name with reference to Survey No.150 Part admeasuring Ac.0.34 cents along with the lands of others.

It is also alleged that the physical possession in respect of the said land was not taken over from the petitioner's father nor the compensation was paid as per the said Award dated 16.08.1982.
3.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that after the demise of petitioner's father, certain disputes arose among the joint family and some litigation in respect of the same is pending.
Be that as it may.

He submits that the issue with regard to acquisition of land in different survey numbers adjacent to Survey No.150 Part of Pernamitta Village and the Award No.111/82 dated 16.08.1982 in respect of the same fell for consideration before a learned Single Judge in W.P.No.11157 of 2009 & batch.

The learned Sri.Ghadiyaram Siddartha Sankar Das vs State Of Ap., Revenue Dept., 4 Others on 8 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84637127/
2

entities.text: Sri.Ghadiyaram Siddartha Sankar Das vs State Of Ap., Revenue Dept., 4 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Judge considering the submissions made by both sides, as also the crucial aspect that there is no proof that an Award was actually passed and that even after an opportunity was given, absolutely no proof was filed to show that the procedure under the Land Acquisition Act was initiated and followed leading to the passing of the Award and vesting of the land in the Government opined  3 that in the absence of any proof, the Court has to hold that the respondent- State failed to prove it's right, title or possession over the subject matter lands.

The learned Judge while allowing the writ petitions declared that the respondent-State cannot rely upon the said Award No.111/82, since there is no record filed to show that an Award was in fact passed.
4. In the present Writ Petition which was filed in the year 2015, no counter has been filed denying the averments made in the affidavit filed in support of the writ petition.

That apart, the land acquisition proceedings in respect of which Award No.111/82 was stated to be passed covering subject matter lands was not approved by the learned Judge in W.P.No.11157 of 2009 &
batch and a Mandamus was issued that the respondent-State cannot rely upon the so called Award No.111/1982.

In the light of the said orders and as it is specifically asserted that the petitioner herein is in possession of land in question, which remained un-rebutted, there shall be a direction to the respondents not to dispossess the petitioner, without initiating land acquisition proceedings.
5. Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed to the extent indicated above.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel, all the pending miscellaneous applications, if any shall stand closed.
